statements.t: We expect to remain in compliance with all covenants under the 2024 Credit Agreement during the twelve-month period following the date of this report based on our current operational and financial projections.

Our current cash and investments, projected cash flows from operations, proceeds from equity or debt issuances, the A/R Agreements and the facilities under our 2024 Credit Agreement are expected to adequately finance our purchase commitments, capital expenditures, acquisitions, scheduled debt service requirements, and all other expected cash requirements for at least the next 12 months.
The level of our outstanding purchase commitments and our expected level of capital expenditures over the next 12 months represent a number of capital programs that are currently underway or planned.
Each of our four reporting segments met or exceeded its targets.
We expect further margin improvement in the fourth quarter, despite a lower SANAD rig count following the suspension of five rigs.
“Our Lower 48 rig count grew as expected, and daily adjusted gross margin again exceeded guidance.
“We anticipate delivering full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA of approximately $930 million, reaching the upper end of our prior guidance.
We now expect full-year consolidated adjusted free cash flow of $100 to $110 million, including approximately $20 million of cash consumption at SANAD.
This revised guidance is materially higher than our previous guidance.
“We now expect full-year consolidated capital spending of $710 to $720 million, including $295 to $305 million for SANAD’s newbuild program.
We expect further sequential adjusted EBITDA growth in the fourth quarter, led by U.S.
We remain on track to achieve an annualized adjusted EBITDA run rate of approximately $1 billion heading into 2027.”

We do not provide a forward-looking reconciliation of our outlook for Segment Adjusted EBITDA, Segment Gross Margin or Adjusted Free Cash Flow, as the amount and significance of items required to develop meaningful comparable GAAP financial measures cannot be estimated at this time without unreasonable efforts.
